transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve just been feeling like I can’t shut off. Like I’m always moving from one thing to the next—at school, at home—and I don’t really settle down in between. It’s like I’m running on a motor.
Can you tell me how old you were when you first started noticing this feeling of always being 'on the go' and unable to settle down?

Pretty young, I think. Elementary school. My mom used to say I was “teaching the class from my seat” because I’d be out of my chair or talking, jumping in before the teacher even finished giving directions. So… it wasn’t new in adulthood or anything.
Do you often find it hard to pay attention or stay focused on tasks, like schoolwork or conversations, even when you're trying to concentrate?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I can usually follow along if I’m trying… sometimes my mind drifts, I guess, but I don’t know if that’s the main thing.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in situations like lines or conversations?

Yeah… I do that. I’ll jump into conversations at work, with colleagues or parents, and at home too. I think I’m helping or moving things along, but I end up talking over people or kind of taking over before they’re finished. It’s… not great.
Do you often lose track of items you need, forget appointments or tasks, or find it hard to stay organized in your daily routine?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say that’s the big issue for me. I mean, I misplace things sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t really thought of it as a pattern. Appointments I usually manage if they’re written down.
Do you often find yourself avoiding or putting off tasks that require sustained mental effort, like paperwork or detailed projects, because they feel tedious or hard to focus on?
I’m not sure. Paperwork isn’t my favorite, but I don’t know that I avoid it because of focus exactly. I usually just try to get through it when I have to.
Do you often feel physically restless or fidgety, like needing to move your hands, tap your feet, or get up when you're supposed to stay seated?

Yeah… I guess I do. In IEP meetings or my admin classes, my leg’s usually bouncing under the table, or I’m clicking a pen. Sometimes I’m shifting around enough that people look over, and I don’t even notice until then.
Would you say these behaviors—jumping in, restlessness—have actually caused problems for you, like conflicts at work or in your personal relationships, in more than one area of your life?

Yeah… unfortunately, yes. At work it’s gotten serious enough that I was put on a corrective plan. I don’t really like talking about that, but it’s there.

And at home… my spouse says the caregiving routines are harder because people have to manage my energy on top of everything else. I’m trying to help, but it feels like I’m damaging trust with colleagues and family.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports childhood-onset (elementary school) pattern of hyperactive-impulsive behavior: motor restlessness, fidgeting/leg bouncing, blurting out answers, interrupting others, and difficulty waiting turn. These behaviors persist into adulthood and cause significant impairment in multiple settings (work corrective action plan, marital/caregiving strain at home). Inattentive symptoms (poor sustained attention, disorganization, losing items, avoidance of effortful tasks) were largely denied or minimized, indicating a hyperactivity/impulsivity-predominant presentation rather than combined or purely inattentive type. Chronicity since childhood, cross-situational impairment, and absence of manic/mood episode features (no euphoria, grandiosity, or episodic course) support ADHD (ICD-10 Disturbance of Activity and Attention) over mood or conduct-related differentials.
